If these agents cannot be tolerated then thorough cleaning with a diluted solution or other partially effective agent is advised.2 In the UK, it is recommended1 that if it is the intention to reuse an endo- scope that has been employed in patients with suspected or confirmed CJD or has been used for invasive procedures in those at risk of CJD (e.g. haemophiliacs), then the endo- scope should be disinfected with a non-aldehyde disinfect- ant (preferably single use) separately from other endo- scopes and quarantined for use only in those with confirmed CJD. Recommendations for disinfection and sterilisation in CJD have also been published in the UK3 and USA.4 1. British Society of Gastroenterology. BSG Working Party Report 2003 (updated 2005).
